opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Andrew Mann (E014) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Write is at or below the maximum, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Andrew Mann (E014): contractor with basic security training. Contractors max at read unless they have advanced training. Requested write is above the maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent's record for Andrew Mann (E014) states he is a contractor with basic security training (both looked up in the security database). Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; they can never be admin. Since he has only basic training, his maximum is read. The requested write is above that maximum, so I grant the maximum: read. (Note: another note claims full-time status, but given the explicit contractor + basic training security record, I apply the more restrictive, evidence-backed maximum of read.)
